body: Looks like @kevva was on the money here: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/34350#issuecomment-1055463916

For your info, I worked around it by mocking them manually in the test files instead:

```js
jest.mock('path/to/image.svg', () => 'svg');
```

However, it'd be nice if we could override/extend the default values in `moduleNameMapper`.
Yeah, thanks to this comment https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/26749#issuecomment-885431747, I got to the same workaround for now. Thanks @kevva
@kevva, did you end up creating an issue for the moduleNameMapper order?
No, unfortunately not. I don't have time for writing a good issue with a good reproduction case atm. Feel free to go ahead and do it :).
(Just to be clear, in my case I can't mock the module as a workaround, I do want to use it in my test)

issue.title: Jest errors with inline SVGs in Next 12.1.1+

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

issue.body:
### Verify canary release - [X] I verified that the issue exists in Next.js canary release ### Provide environment information Operating System: Platform: darwin Arch: x64 Version: Darwin Kernel Version 20.6.0: Wed Jan 12 22:22:42 PST 2022; root:xnu-7195.141.19~2/RELEASE_X86_64 Binaries: Node: 16.14.2 npm: 8.5.0 Yarn: 1.22.18 pnpm: N/A Relevant packages: next: 12.1.6-canary.3 react: 17.0.2 react-dom: 17.0.2 ### What browser are you using? (if relevant) _No response_ ### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant) _No response_ ### Describe the Bug When using SVGR (or presumably any other Webpack-based SVG importing library) and inline rendering the imported SVG, I encounter errors in Jest when running tests: ``` Warning: React.jsx: type is invalid -- expected a string (for built-in components) or a class/function (for composite components) but got: object. ``` A minimal example of inline rendering an imported SVG (as opposed to utilizing next/image): ``` import Vercel from '../public/vercel.svg' export default function Home() { return (

Welcome to Next.js!

) } ``` This is because the next build tool which provides the Jest configuration includes this `moduleNameMapper` [rule](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/3c1515953d808a1296dd6d1e06e2f1d6ace4d888/packages/next/build/jest/jest.ts#L89): ``` // Handle image imports '^.+\\.(png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp|avif|ico|bmp|svg)$': require.resolve( `./__mocks__/fileMock.js` ), ``` This fileMock resolver provides an object which is meant to be supplied to a Next `` component. But in my use case I want to directly render the SVG without next/image. There is no way to override this image import rule for SVGs in my own jest.config.js. Related issues: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/34350#issuecomment-1055463916 https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/33161 https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/26167 ### Expected Behavior Next should provide a configuration option to exclude SVGs from being mocked this way in Jest. ### To Reproduce Repo with reproduction code: https://github.com/rsanchez-forks/next-with-jest-and-svgr ``` git clone git@github.com:rsanchez-forks/next-with-jest-and-svgr.git cd next-with-jest-and-svgr npm install npm test ```

issue.title: next/jest: Allow moduleNameMapper to match before Next.js internal mappings
issue.body:
Fixes #35634

This change doesn't require tests as importing svgs is not a supported feature, this just makes it slightly more ergonomic to override the matchers.

body: I've moved the moduleNameMapper so that you can override the mapping. The case where you want to do anything else than is provided by default is explained well by @xveganxxxedgex's comment: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/35634#issuecomment-1080942525. That approach allows you to override any setting you'd want to tweak based on customizations you've done to the webpack config, those are not covered / supported by Next.js and as such are not specifically added as features to next/jest.
I'm still experiencing this issue in Next v12.1.6 with Jest v28.0.3. I'm currently using the solution proposed by @timmywil as a workaround.

issue.title: [Bug]: Jest testing failed for `next@12.1.6`

repository.name: blog
repository.description: :rocket: An awesome blog system based on Next.js

issue.body:
## **Describe the bug**

Jest testing failed when bump `next` version from `12.1.5` to `12.1.6`. 

## **To Reproduce**

Failed CI report [here](https://github.com/sabertazimi/blog/runs/6326792660?check_suite_focus=true).

## **Expected behavior**

Jest CI pass.

## **Additional context**

Possible reason see vercel/next.js#36312:

`next@12.1.6` changed `moduleNameMapper` configuration.

More details see vercel/next.js#36682 and vercel/next.js#35634.
